hero.oneLiner: Incorporated in 1985, a power distribution infrastructure services provider offering operation and maintenance (O&M) and allied support services primarily to electricity distribution utilities in India.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: Incorporated in 1985, a power distribution infrastructure services provider offering operation and maintenance (O&M) and allied support services primarily to electricity distribution utilities in India.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: The Company provides operation, maintenance and field-level execution of works relating to electricity distribution networks and associated infrastructure, including distribution lines, feeders, substations, poles and cables. Operations are organised into three service verticals: Network O&M Services, Electrical Infrastructure and Network Development Works, and Metering and Meter Management Services. Contracts are typically awarded through competitive tenders by electricity distribution utilities under rate contracts, outline agreements or annual maintenance contracts, with work orders issued from time to time; private sector clients may award work directly.

group_structure.title: Group structure (subsidiaries / JV / related parties)
group_structure.body:
- Pravi Facilities Solutions LLP — Other venture of Promoters Jawed Akhtar and Sunil Lakshman Vatsa: Disclosed as an LLP interest of both Promoter-Directors
- Vatsa Electric Private Limited — Other directorship of Promoter and Managing Director Sunil Lakshman Vatsa
- Group Companies — None: As on date of the Red Herring Prospectus, there are no companies falling under the definition of SEBI (ICDR) Regulations, 2018 to be identified as group companies

products.title: Products & brands
products.body:
- **Network Operation and Maintenance (O&M) Services:** Maintenance and operational support of electrical distribution systems across 33 kV, 11 kV and low-tension (LT) networks, O&M support for 33/11 kV substations, Deployment of technical manpower for line maintenance, network inspection and fault rectification, System monitoring, fault detection, troubleshooting and repair of distribution networks and substations, Installation, testing and commissioning of distribution systems across 33 kV, 11 kV, HT and LT networks
- **Electrical Infrastructure and Network Development Works:** Pole-related works including erection and shifting of poles, Cable-related works including laying, jointing and termination of underground and overhead cables, Installation of distribution network components, Civil works such as excavation, foundation works, construction of plinths and other supporting civil structures
- **Metering and Meter Management Services:** Installation and replacement of energy meters, Meter testing, Meter reading, Other related metering support activities

cost_leadership.title: Supply chain integration (RHP report)
cost_leadership.body: The Company does not undertake in-house manufacturing of electrical equipment and does not own or operate any manufacturing facilities or significant plant and machinery; its operations are primarily contract-based. It procures electrical materials, equipment, consumables and spares required across its three service verticals from third-party manufacturers and suppliers on a project-specific basis, in accordance with project specifications, technical standards, tender conditions and contractual requirements. Materials procured typically include power and control cables, busbars, switchgear, circuit breakers, panels, protection and control systems, insulators, structural components and allied electrical accessories for the Electrical Infrastructure and Network Development Works vertical, and consumables, tools, spares and replacement components for the Network O&M and Metering verticals. Service verticals are executed through deployment of manpower, engagement of subcontractors, and use of tools and equipment at project sites. The Company does not maintain a centralised warehouse or centralised inventory facility; materials are generally delivered directly to project sites or stored at site-level facilities for the duration of the project, with inventory managed on a project-wise basis. Logistics operations are carried out through a combination of Company-owned vehicles (monitored through GPS-based systems) and third-party service providers. The Company intends to strengthen vendor and subcontractor networks and enhance project planning, procurement and inventory management systems.

demand_drivers.title: Seasonality (RHP report)
demand_drivers.body: Our business is not subject to seasonality.

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Expansion of the Electrical Infrastructure and Network Development Works vertical, participating in tenders and work orders for development, augmentation and strengthening of electricity distribution infrastructure
- Geographic expansion and deeper penetration in existing regions by increasing participation in projects across additional states and regions, including bidding in regions witnessing investment in power distribution strengthening
- Deploying project teams and manpower closer to project sites and establishing temporary site facilities to support execution across locations
- Strengthening project delivery and execution readiness by enhancing project planning, procurement and inventory management systems, improving mobilisation of manpower and strengthening vendor and subcontractor arrangements

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: The DRHP describes expansion in terms of service verticals and geography rather than plant or manufacturing capacity. The Company proposes to expand its Electrical Infrastructure and Network Development Works vertical (14.66%, 7.67% and 13.53% of revenue from operations in Fiscals 2026, 2025 and 2024 respectively) by participating in tenders and work orders for development, augmentation and strengthening of electricity distribution infrastructure. It also intends to expand its geographical presence into additional states and regions - currently Odisha accounts for 69.05% of Fiscal 2026 revenue, with Maharashtra 12.45%, Delhi 7.56%, Gujarat 6.63%, Rajasthan 3.61%, Uttar Pradesh 0.64% and Goa 0.07% - while continuing in markets with prior execution experience, supported by deployment of project teams closer to project sites and establishment of temporary site facilities. Any such expansion is stated to be subject to availability of suitable tender opportunities, successful award of contracts and timely execution.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Presence across electrical infrastructure activities with major revenue from O&M services, spanning three service verticals (O&M 76.90% of revenue from operations in Fiscal 2026)
- Order book providing revenue visibility - 34 ongoing projects with unexecuted value of approximately Rs. 553.70 crores as of June 30, 2026, primarily from electricity distribution utilities
- Majority of revenue from repetitive customers - 88.29% in FY 2025-26, 97.14% in FY 2024-25 and 99.28% in FY 2023-24
- Experienced management team and manpower strength - 4,473 employees as of May 31, 2026 (4,332 permanent and 141 contractual), led by two promoter-directors each with over 30 years of experience
- Recurring/periodic billing under annual maintenance contracts and rate contracts, as compared to project-based execution, providing revenue visibility over the contract duration

risks.title: Bear — key risks
risks.body:
- Customer-segment concentration on power distribution utilities — A major portion of revenue is derived from electricity distribution utilities (79.10% of revenue from operations in Fiscal 2026, 88.73% in Fiscal 2025, 88.87% in Fiscal 2024); any reduction in business from such customers, adverse changes in procurement practices or failure to secure new contracts may adversely affect business, results of operations, financial condition and cash flows
- Dependence on sector capital expenditure, government policy and schemes such as RDSS — Demand for the Company's services is directly linked to the level of investment in electricity distribution infrastructure, which is influenced by capital expenditure programmes of utilities, availability of funding, government policies and reforms, and implementation of sectoral schemes such as the Revamped Distribution Sector Scheme
- Regulated counterparties with constrained financial position and investment capacity — Electricity distribution utilities operate within a regulated framework and are subject to approval processes and performance requirements prescribed by regulatory authorities; their financial position and investment capacity affect the Company
- Order book conversion risk — Realization of revenues from the order book of approximately Rs. 553.70 crores is subject to commencement and progress of projects, issuance of work orders, site availability, customer approvals and other factors beyond the Company's control; there can be no assurance the entire order book will convert into revenue within expected timelines or at all
- Geographic concentration — Odisha contributed 69.05%, 74.52% and 67.09% of revenue from operations in Fiscals 2026, 2025 and 2024 respectively, leaving revenue exposed to a single state's distribution capex and tendering
- Dependence on competitive tendering and repeat orders — Contracts are typically awarded through competitive tender processes; ability to continue receiving repeat orders depends on performance of existing contracts, customer requirements, competitive bidding and other external factors, and repeat-customer revenue share has declined from 99.28% (FY 2023-24) to 88.29% (FY 2025-26)
- Manpower-intensive operations in high-voltage environments — Execution depends on deployment of a 4,473-person workforce (as of May 31, 2026) of supervisors, linemen, technicians and helpers across designated service areas, supported by vehicles, tools and equipment, with defined operating procedures required for high-voltage work
